title.en: Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America amid Canada trade war – US politics live
title.zh: 特朗普签署命令将安大略湖更名为“美利坚湖”，正值与加拿大贸易战之际——美国政治直播

summary.en: The President has reportedly signed an order to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America, amidst ongoing tensions and a trade dispute with Canada. This action is part of a broader context of the President's public criticism of Canada and other international policy decisions, including a temporary suspension of beef tariffs...
summary.zh: 据报道，总统签署了一项命令，将安大略湖更名为“美利坚湖”，此举正值与加拿大持续紧张的贸易争端之际。这一行动是总统公开批评加拿大及其他国际政策决定的一部分，其中包括暂时中止牛肉关税，旨在降低食品杂货成本。

body.en: President hits out at Canada as he makes latest attempt to rename a landmark Exclusive: Trump’s war on Iran is rapidly draining US navy budget Exclusive: RFK Jr lied in Senate confirmation hearings, newly revealed documents indicate Sign up for the Breaking News US email On Wednesday, Trump officially signed a proclamation on Wednesday that suspends higher tariffs on 300,000 metric tons of foreign beef imports for 90 days. This comes after backlash to the proposal – designed to lower grocery costs for Americans in the run-up to the November midterms. Several Republicans – in states with sizable cattle farming industries – have criticized the policy, saying it is a short term solution that will stymie ranchers’ ability to rebuild their herds. Four leading livestock and agricultural organizations also wrote a letter to the president on Wednesday urging him to reverse course. “Flooding the market with discounted foreign beef is not the way to rebuild the American cattle herd, strengthen food security, or lower grocery bills in a lasting way,” the groups wrote. Donald Trump will begin his day in Washington, before traveling to Houston, Texas where he’ll headline a Republican National Commitee (RNC) fundraiser, and help boost Ken Paxton — the state’s attorney general and Republican nominee for Senate. A reminder that Paxton beat long serving Senator John Cornyn in the GOP primary earlier this year after receiving Trump’s endorsement. Paxton is set to face Democratic state lawmaker James Talarico in November. Continue reading...
body.zh: 总统猛烈抨击加拿大，试图重新命名具有里程碑意义的建筑 独家：特朗普对伊朗的战争正在迅速耗尽美国海军预算 独家：小罗伯特·肯尼迪在参议院确认听证会上撒谎，新披露的文件显示周三，特朗普正式签署了一项公告，暂停对 30 万吨外国牛肉进口征收更高的关税，为期 90 天。此前，该提案遭到强烈反对，该提案旨在在 11 月中期选举前降低美国人的食品杂货成本。几位共和党人——在拥有规模化养牛业的州——批评了这项政策，称这是一个短期解决方案，将阻碍牧场主重建牛群的能力。四个主要畜牧业和农业组织周三也致信总统，敦促他改变做法。这些组织写道：“用打折的外国牛肉充斥市场并不是重建美国牛群、加强粮食安全或持久降低食品杂货费用的方法。”唐纳德·特朗普将在华盛顿开始新的一天，然后前往德克萨斯州休斯顿，在那里他将主持共和党全国委员会 (RNC) 筹款活动，并帮助推动该州总检察长、共和党参议员候选人肯·帕克斯顿 (Ken Paxton)。提醒人们的是，帕克斯顿在获得特朗普的支持后，在今年早些时候的共和党初选中击败了长期任职的参议员约翰·科宁。帕克斯顿将于 11 月迎战民主党州议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科 (James Talarico)。继续阅读...

Romans 12:18 calls us to live peaceably with all, emphasizing our own responsibility in fostering harmony. In a world where nations share borders and resources, striving for...
reflection.zh: 一位领导人试图将安大略湖改名，并在贸易争端中“抨击加拿大”的消息，凸显了维持和平国际关系的挑战。罗马书12:18呼吁我们尽力与众人和睦，强调我们自己在促进和谐方面的责任。在一个国家共享边界和资源的世界里，即使存在分歧，努力争取相互尊重和缓和局势也是一项至关重要的追求。

title.en: Nepal flash flood: more than 350 killed amid warning of fresh danger from rising lake water – latest updates
title.zh: 尼泊尔山洪突发更新：冰川崩塌致藏边界百余人失踪

summary.en: At least 165 people have died following a flash flood caused by a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border. Hundreds of foreign nationals from various countries are among the missing. Eyewitnesses on the Tibetan side described trees and electricity poles being knocked down by the rapidly advancing floodwaters.
summary.zh: 由于冰川崩塌引发的山洪暴发，已造成至少165人死亡。来自多个国家的数百名外国公民失踪。在边境的藏族一侧，目击者描述了洪水冲倒树木和电线杆的场景。

body.en: Authorities say water rising at lake at site of disaster and it could burst Nearly 1,400 missing, mostly tourists, and hundreds killed Visual guide: how the deadly flooding unfolded Tell us: have you been affected by the flash floods? Eyewitness accounts have been emerging from the Tibetan side of the border , with a woman saying she was travelling from Gyirong town towards Nepal on Wednesday morning when her group encountered the flood about 4km from Gyirong port. “Trees and electricity poles had already been knocked down, and the flood water was bearing down on us. We didn’t dare turn around, so we could only reverse,” the woman, surnamed Fang, told Xiaoxiang Morning News . I was really scared. My whole body was trembling. Continue reading...
body.zh: 至少有 165 人死亡，官员称失踪者中有数百名来自印度、美国、英国、澳大利亚、马来西亚和乌克兰的外国人。关注最新消息 尼藏边境山洪造成数十人死亡、数百人失踪 告诉我们：您受到山洪影响了吗？来自边境西藏一侧的目击者称，一名妇女称，周三早上她从吉隆镇前往尼泊尔，当时她的团队在距离吉隆口岸约 4 公里处遭遇了洪水。 “树木、电线杆都被冲倒了，洪水向我们扑来，我们不敢掉头，只能倒车。”方女士告诉潇湘晨报。我真的很害怕。我的整个身体都在颤抖。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The devastating flash flood in Nepal, triggered by a glacial collapse, serves as a stark reminder of the immense power of natural forces and the fragility of human life. The earth itself, in its current state, groans under the weight of sin and decay, a reality that touches us all through such tragic events. In these moments of overwhelming loss, we are...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔因冰川崩塌引发的毁灭性山洪，是对自然力量的巨大威力以及人类生命脆弱性的严峻提醒。大地本身在其现状下，因罪恶和败坏而呻吟，这一现实通过如此悲惨的事件触及我们所有人。在这些压倒性的损失时刻，我们被呼召与哀痛者一同哀哭，并持守未来复兴的盼望。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Climate crisis could be destabilising mountain areas like Nepal, experts warn
title.zh: 专家警告：气候危机可能正在破坏尼泊尔等山区稳定

summary.en: Experts warn that unusual heat this year may have melted ice and thawed bonds holding glaciers in place, potentially destabilizing mountain areas like Nepal. A devastating flash flood, caused by a glacier collapse in the Himalayas, ripped through border communities in Nepal and Tibet, sweeping away buildings and...
summary.zh: 专家警告称，今年异常高温可能融化了冰川，使其固定结构松动，从而破坏了尼泊尔等山区的稳定。喜马拉雅山脉冰川崩塌引发的毁灭性山洪，冲毁了尼泊尔和西藏边境社区的建筑物和道路，造成至少360人死亡，1400人失踪。

body.en: Unusual heat this year may have melted ice and thawed bonds that hold glaciers in place – leading to catastrophe Nepal-Tibet flash flood – latest updates What caused the flash flood in Nepal and Tibet? The devastating flash flood that has ripped through the border communities of Nepal and Tibet has heightened fears that the climate crisis is destabilising the geology of mountain and polar regions, threatening millions of people. Satellite imagery suggests a glacier collapse high in the Himalayas was the primary cause of the deadly torrent of mud, water and ice that tore along the Bhotekoshi River on Wednesday. It swept away buildings and roads and left at least 360 dead and 1,400 missing. Continue reading...
body.zh: 今年异常炎热的天气可能会融化冰层并解冻固定冰川的债券，从而导致灾难 尼泊尔-西藏山洪 - 最新动态 是什么导致了尼泊尔和西藏的山洪？席卷尼泊尔和西藏边境社区的毁灭性山洪加剧了人们的担忧，即气候危机正在破坏山区和极地的地质稳定，威胁着数百万人。卫星图像显示，喜马拉雅山高处的冰川崩塌是周三博特科希河沿岸致命的泥浆、水和冰流的主要原因。它冲毁了建筑物和道路，造成至少 360 人死亡、1,400 人失踪。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The devastating flash flood in Nepal and Tibet, caused by a glacier collapse linked to unusual heat, serves as a stark reminder of creation's vulnerability. As the earth experiences environmental destabilization, we witness the profound suffering and loss, with at least 360 dead and 1,400 missing in this tragedy. Yahweh's word reminds us that the whole...
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔和西藏发生的毁灭性山洪，源于异常高温导致的冰川崩塌，这严酷地提醒我们受造界的脆弱。当大地经历环境失稳时，我们目睹了深重的苦难和损失，这场悲剧中至少有360人死亡，1400人失踪。雅伟的话语提醒我们，整个受造界都在呻吟，渴望从其所承受的重担中得到更新和复原。

The prime minister wrote to a campaigner in May outlining his support for a £500,000 individual donations cap, which he said would “guard against the perception of any one party being unduly influenced or swayed by one person or organisation”. Continue reading...

title.en: Key moments in trial of Lindsay Clancy, the mother accused of murdering her three children
title.zh: 被指控谋杀三个孩子的母亲林赛·克兰西受审的关键时刻

summary.en: A jury is deliberating in the trial of the Massachusetts mother charged with murdering her three small children
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A jury is deliberating in the trial of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother charged with murdering her three small children at their home in suburban Boston.

In a case that has captivated the American public, Clancy has not disputed that she killed them, but her lawyers argue she should not be held legally responsible because she was suffering from severe mental illness.

Clancy is charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the January 2023 deaths. If convicted by a jury, she faces life in prison without parole.

Prosecutors allege that on 24 January 2023, Clancy intentionally strangled all of her children - Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, eight months - with fitness bands in their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home before jumping from a second-floor window. Clancy, now 36, was paralysed by the fall and attended the trial in a wheelchair.

Clancy's attorneys, while defending her, have never rejected her role in the killings.

Instead, they have put forth a defence of insanity, arguing that Clancy had hallucinations and delusions after giving birth to her youngest child. They pointed to treatment for mental health problems and that she checked herself into a psychiatric hospital just days before the deaths.

Prosecutors, meanwhile, have argued Clancy made a calculated decision to intentionally kill her children and should be held legally responsible. They allege that at the time, Clancy sent her husband, Patrick Clancy, out on errands so that he would not be home.

Clancy's family, including her former mother-in-law and husband, have testified about her mental state leading up to the deaths.

The five-week trial has sparked interest on social media as thousands watched the court proceedings. Hundreds of women have showed up outside the courthouse to support Clancy, wearing pink shirts with phrases like "She Needed Help" and "Peace For Lindsay".

Over two days, Clancy's ex-husband, Patrick, told jurors about his ex-wife's declining mental health after giving birth and described the day his children died in gruesome detail.

He told jurors that Clancy's "big spiral" began about a month before their deaths.

"She started to lose a lot of weight, and she became very depressed, and she was having a really hard time," he said.

He described her intermittently seeking help from doctors and taking a variety of medications, adding that he recalled her saying she was starting to have thoughts of suicide.

Patrick Clancy described his last image of son Dawson sitting on the couch eating chicken nuggets before he left to get food and medication. He came back to find his children dead.

Lindsay Clancy sobbed in court as a recording of her husband's 911 call played. He can be heard screaming, "She killed the kids", after finding their children in the...
body.zh: 陪审团正在审议对马萨诸塞州母亲林赛·克兰西的审判，她被指控在波士顿郊区的家中谋杀了她的三个小孩。 在这起引起美国公众关注的案件中，克兰西并没有否认她杀害了他们，但她的律师认为，她不应该承担法律责任，因为她患有严重的精神疾病。 克兰西在 2023 年 1 月的死亡事件中被指控犯有三项一级谋杀罪。如果陪审团定罪，她将面临终身监禁且不得假释。 检察官称，2023 年 1 月 24 日，克兰西在马萨诸塞州达克斯伯里的家中故意用健身带勒死了她所有的孩子——5 岁的科拉、3 岁的道森和 8 个月大的卡兰，然后从二楼的窗户跳下。现年 36 岁的克兰西因摔倒而瘫痪，坐在轮椅上参加了审判。 克兰西的律师在为她辩护的同时，从未否认她在杀戮中所扮演的角色。 相反，他们提出了精神错乱的辩护，认为克兰西在生下最小的孩子后出现了幻觉和妄想。他们指出，她接受了精神健康问题的治疗，并且在死亡前几天她曾到精神病院接受检查。 与此同时，检察官认为克兰西做出了故意杀害孩子的深思熟虑的决定，应该承担法律责任。他们声称，当时克兰西派她的丈夫帕特里克·克兰西出去办事，这样他就不在家。 克兰西的家人，包括她的前婆婆和丈夫，已经就她死亡前的精神状态作证。 为期五周的审判引起了社交媒体的关注，数千人观看了法庭审理过程。数百名女性出现在法院外支持克兰西，她们穿着粉红色衬衫，上面写着“她需要帮助”和“林赛和平”等字样。 两天多的时间里，克兰西的前夫帕特里克向陪审员讲述了他的前妻在生完孩子后心理健康状况每况愈下的情况，并详细描述了他的孩子们死亡的那一天。 他告诉陪审员，克兰西的“大螺旋”大约在他们去世前一个月开始。 “她的体重开始下降，她变得非常沮丧，她的日子非常难过，”他说。 他描述了她断断续续地寻求医生的帮助并服用各种药物，并补充说他记得她说她开始有自杀的念头。 帕特里克·克兰西描述了他儿子道森在离开去买食物和药物之前坐在沙发上吃鸡块的最后一张照片。他回来发现他的孩子们都死了。 法庭上播放着她丈夫拨打 911 电话的录音，林赛·克兰西 (Lindsay Clancy) 在法庭上抽泣。在发现他们的孩子后，可以听到他尖叫着，“她杀了孩子们”。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

title.en: Allan Little: I met dangerously fanatical Mladić early in Bosnian war
title.zh: 艾伦·利特尔：我在波斯尼亚战争初期遇到了危险狂热的姆拉迪奇

summary.en: BBC special correspondent Allan Little met the "Butcher of Bosnia" in the early months of the Bosnian war.

body.en:
Bosnian Serb commander Ratko Mladić, dubbed the "Butcher of Bosnia" for his actions during the Balkan wars of the 1990s, has died in prison.

BBC special correspondent Allan Little was there throughout the breakup of the former Yugoslavia, and met Mladić in the early months of the Bosnian war.

At night, you could watch the fires of ethnic cleansing across the landscape. The flames provided the only light under the night sky and the black valley would glimmer with flecks of orange.

You could watch the men of our village move about silently in the shadows of their homes, each armed with some ancient weapon salvaged from wars long ago and, like the fears and the suspicions and the distrusts, handed down through the generations.

One morning I watched a procession of men and women emerge from a forest. They had been driven from their homes two days earlier and had fled with what they could carry.

Most were on foot. Some were crammed into the back of ancient farm vehicles drawn by donkeys. There were perhaps 40,000 of them. Their home town had fallen to a Serb advance that had come without warning.

The whole town had fled, he said. He had become separated from his wife in the long trek to safety and was now worried that she had not made it. His pale, almost translucently white skin was stretched across the bones of his face like parchment. His forehead was livid blue from a fall.

I asked him how old he was. He said he was 80. "May I ask" I said, "are you a Croat or a Muslim?"

The memory of it shames me even now as I hear, in my mind, his answer echo down the years.

Our convenient ethnic shorthand reduced them to Serbs, Croats and Muslims. But they were also musicians and scientists and doctors and plumbers and farmers and mothers and fathers and brothers and sisters and very often children.

I met Mladić in that first hot summer of the war in Bosnia. We were at Lukavica barracks on the southern edge of Sarajevo. The barracks was awash with weapons and the menacing strut of the paramilitaries.

You could buy a Kalashnikov for 200 dollars, a hand grenade for just one dollar – the same price, I would soon learn, as the cost of a fresh egg in the besieged city.

I shook his hand and he held it fast and pulled me in close. He told me he had just come back from the Sarajevo city centre front line and I saw that he was pumped up by the exhilarating proximity of the fighting.

He held my hand for many minutes, fixed me with his eye and told me he was the great defender of brotherhood and unity in former Yugoslavia, and that he dreamed of a world in which there would no guns and no war. He struck me then as fanatical, dangerously so.

In the years that lay ahead, forces under his command committed the worst war crimes on European soil since the Nazis. They...
body.zh: 波斯尼亚塞族指挥官拉特科·姆拉迪奇 (Ratko Mladić) 因在 20 世纪 90 年代巴尔干战争中的所作所为而被称为“波斯尼亚屠夫”，现已在监狱中去世。 BBC 特约记者艾伦·利特尔在前南斯拉夫解体期间一直在那里，并在波斯尼亚战争的最初几个月会见了姆拉迪奇。 到了晚上，你可以看到整个地区种族清洗的火焰。火焰是夜空下唯一的光亮，黑色的山谷闪烁着橙色的斑点。 你可以看到我们村里的男人们在自家的阴影里默默地走动，每个人都拿着一些很久以前从战争中抢救出来的古老武器，就像恐惧、怀疑和不信任一样，代代相传。 一天早上，我看到一队男人和女人从森林里走出来。两天前，他们被赶出了家门，带着能携带的东西逃走了。 大多数人都是步行的。有些人被塞进由驴拉的古老农用车辆的后座上。其中大约有四万人。他们的家乡已被毫无预兆的塞尔维亚人攻陷。 他说，整个城镇都逃走了。在前往安全地带的长途跋涉中，他与妻子失散了，现在他担心她没能成功。他苍白得近乎半透明的皮肤像羊皮纸一样覆盖在脸上的骨头上。他的额头因跌倒而变成青蓝色。 我问他几岁了。他说他已经 80 岁了。“请问，”我说，“你是克罗地亚人还是穆斯林？” 即使现在，当我听到他的答案在我脑海中回响时，这件事的记忆仍然让我感到羞愧。 我们方便的民族速记将他们简化为塞尔维亚人、克罗地亚人和穆斯林。但他们也是音乐家、科学家、医生、水管工、农民、母亲、父亲、兄弟姐妹，而且常常是孩子。 我在波斯尼亚战争第一个炎热的夏天遇见了姆拉迪奇。我们当时在萨拉热窝南部边缘的卢卡维察军营。军营里堆满了武器，准军事人员气势汹汹。 你可以花 200 美元购买一把卡拉什尼科夫冲锋枪，一美元就能买到一枚手榴弹——我很快就了解到，这个价格与被围困的城市中一个新鲜鸡蛋的价格相同。 我握着他的手，他紧紧握住我的手，把我拉近。他告诉我，他刚刚从萨拉热窝市中心前线回来，我看到他因近距离的战斗而感到振奋。 他握着我的手好几分钟，用眼睛盯着我，告诉我他是前南斯拉夫兄弟情谊和团结的伟大捍卫者，他梦想着一个没有枪支、没有战争的世界。当时我觉得他很狂热，甚至很危险。 在接下来的几年里，他指挥下的部队在欧洲土地上犯下了自纳粹以来最严重的战争罪行。他们...

title.en: Norwegians lay flowers at palace as King Harald's condition worsens
title.zh: 哈拉尔国王病情恶化，挪威人向宫殿献花

summary.en: The 89-year-old's condition is described as "extremely serious" and members of his family have visited him in hospital.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Norwegians have laid flowers in front of the palace in Oslo after the royal household said King Harald V's condition in hospital had become "extremely serious".

His wife, Queen Sonja, and his son, Crown Prince Haakon, cancelled royal engagements to be at his bedside at Oslo University Hospital with other members of the family.

They all stayed for several hours, and then during the evening Haakon was seen returning with Crown Princess Mette-Marit.

The 89-year-old has been in hospital for 10 days receiving treatment for a rare blood condition, haemolytic anaemia. Late on Thursday afternoon the palace issued an update to say his condition was unchanged.

Having been on the throne since 1991, King Harald is Europe's oldest head of state.

Crown Prince Haakon, 53, the successor to the Norwegian throne, has been serving as regent while his father is on leave.

King Harald has been treated in recent weeks with cortisone for haemolytic anaemia, a condition that causes the number of red blood cells in the body to be reduced, and leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.

There was a sombre mood in Oslo as Norwegians followed the comings and goings of the royal family. Crowds milled around in Palace Square throughout the day as Norwegian public TV scrapped its schedule to cover the story.

Although no-one in the royal family spoke, the message was clear that it had become an important moment to visit the king.

Among those visiting the hospital were Crown Princess Mette-Marit who arrived with Haakon, as well as her son Marius Borg Høiby, who is under house arrest during his appeal against a conviction for rape.

King Harald's sister, Princess Astrid, also visited the hospital, along with Haakon and Mette-Marit's children Princess Ingrid Alexandra and Prince Sverre Magnus.

Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre cancelled a planned trip to Germany, where he was expected to meet Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Thursday.

"The whole nation is with us as we send warm thoughts to the king and the rest of the royal family," he said in a statement.

The king has had multiple health problems in recent years which have forced him to scale back his royal duties.

He was fitted with a pacemaker in 2024 after falling ill on holiday in Malaysia.

Crown Princess Mette-Marit received a lung transplant in June after she had been diagnosed with a rare form of pulmonary fibrosis in 2018.

The transplant came two days after Høiby was sentenced to four years in prison after being convicted of two counts of rape. He had denied the most serious charges and is to appeal the sentence.

Høiby, 29, was four when his mother married Crown Prince Haakon and is not himself a royal figure.

body.zh: 在王室表示哈拉尔五世国王在医院的病情变得“极其严重”后，挪威人在奥斯陆宫殿前献花。 他的妻子索尼娅王后和儿子哈康王储取消了皇室活动，与其他家庭成员一起在奥斯陆大学医院的床边陪伴他。 他们都呆了几个小时，然后在晚上哈康与王储妃梅特·玛丽特一起回来。 这位 89 岁的老人已经住院 10 天，接受一种罕见的血液疾病——溶血性贫血的治疗。周四下午晚些时候，白金汉宫发布了最新消息，称他的病情没有变化。 哈拉尔国王自 1991 年即位以来，是欧洲最年长的国家元首。 53岁的挪威王位继承人哈康王储在父亲休假期间一直担任摄政王。 哈拉尔国王最近几周接受了可的松治疗溶血性贫血，这种疾病会导致体内红细胞数量减少，并导致疲劳和呼吸短促。 挪威人关注着王室成员的出入，奥斯陆气氛阴沉。由于挪威公共电视台取消了节目播出时间来报道这一事件，一整天人群都在宫殿广场上转来转去。 尽管王室中没有人发声，但传达的信息很明确：现在已经成为拜访国王的重要时刻。 与哈康一起抵达医院的王储妃梅特·玛丽特以及她的儿子马吕斯·博格·霍伊比均到医院探访，后者在对强奸定罪提出上诉期间被软禁。 哈拉尔国王的妹妹阿斯特丽德公主以及哈康和梅特玛丽特的孩子英格丽德·亚历山德拉公主和斯韦雷·马格努斯王子也参观了医院。 总理乔纳斯·加尔·斯托尔取消了原定的德国之行，预计他将于周四与德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨会面。 他在一份声明中说：“当我们向国王和王室其他成员表达温暖的思念时，整个国家都与我们站在一起。” 近年来，国王出现了多种健康问题，迫使他缩减了王室职责。 2024 年，他在马来西亚度假时生病，并于 2024 年安装了心脏起搏器。 王储妃梅特-玛丽特在 2018 年被诊断出患有一种罕见的肺纤维化后，于 6 月接受了肺移植手术。 移植手术是在霍伊比因两项强奸罪被判四年监禁后两天进行的。他否认了最严重的指控，并对判决提出上诉。 29 岁的霍伊比 (Høiby) 四岁时，他的母亲与哈康王储结婚，霍伊比本人并不是王室成员。 同样在今年早些时候，公布的文件显示梅特-玛丽特与已故的......

title.en: Two killed in 'domestic violence incident' at school near Berlin
title.zh: 柏林附近学校“家庭暴力事件”造成两人死亡

summary.en: Police have arrested a 19-year-old male suspect after an incident in which two people were killed near the German capital.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two people have been killed in a "domestic violence incident" at a school in the town of Gosen-Neu Zittau near the German capital Berlin, local police have said.

Brandenburg state police said they arrested a 19-year-old German man, who is "considered a prime suspect". They said it was not a "mass shooting", without specifying what weapon was used.

One of the dead was an 18-year-old secondary school female student and the other victim was a 30-year-old man who died when he tried to intervene, local media reported.

The arrested suspect is believed to be the ex-boyfriend of the 18-year-old victim, Maz Online reported.

Ulrike Liedtke, the speaker of Brandenburg's regional parliament, called the incident a "cowardly femicide".

"The fact that we once again had to witness deadly violence against a woman fills me with deep sorrow and anger.

"I am shaken that a citizen who showed moral courage and wanted to help also lost his life in this terrible act," Liedtke said.

The school's managing director Michael Kunz said classes will be cancelled on Friday.

Although there would be no regular classes, Kunz said the school would remain open for all students who wished to come.

"We want to provide them with a safe space where they can come together, talk to each other, and process what has happened," he said.

A "very careful" decision will be made in coming days about how school life will be structured, he added.

Last month in a separate attack, two girls were seriously wounded and a 16-year-old suspect arrested at a secondary school in southern Germany.
body.zh: 当地警方称，德国首都柏林附近的戈森-新齐陶镇一所学校发生“家庭暴力事件”，造成两人死亡。 勃兰登堡州警方表示，他们逮捕了一名 19 岁的德国男子，他“被认为是主要嫌疑人”。他们表示这不是“大规模枪击事件”，但没有具体说明使用了什么武器。 据当地媒体报道，其中一名死者是一名 18 岁的中学生，另一名受害者是一名 30 岁的男子，他在试图干预时死亡。 据 Maz Online 报道，被捕嫌疑人据信是 18 岁受害者的前男友。 勃兰登堡地区议会议长乌尔里克·利特克(Ulrike Liedtke)称这起事件是“懦弱的杀害女性事件”。 “我们再次目睹针对一名妇女的致命暴力，这一事实让我感到深深的悲伤和愤怒。 利特克说：“令我震惊的是，一位表现出道德勇气并愿意提供帮助的公民也在这一可怕的行为中丧生。” 学校董事总经理迈克尔·昆兹(Michael Kunz)表示，周五的课程将被取消。 昆茨表示，尽管不会正常上课，但学校将继续向所有希望来的学生开放。 他说：“我们希望为他们提供一个安全的空间，让他们可以聚在一起，互相交谈，并处理所发生的事情。” 他补充说，未来几天将就如何安排学校生活做出“非常谨慎”的决定。 上个月，在德国南部一所中学的另一次袭击中，两名女孩受重伤，一名 16 岁嫌疑人被捕。

title.en: Convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Mladić dies aged 84
title.zh: 被定罪的波斯尼亚塞族战犯姆拉迪奇去世，享年 84 岁

summary.en: He was jailed for life in 2017 for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity during the wars in the ex-Yugoslavia in 1992-95.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Convicted Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladić has died in a UN prison at The Hague aged 84.

He was jailed for life in 2017 for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity during the wars in the former Yugoslavia in 1992-95.

After the Bosnian war, he went on the run for 16 years until he was finally tracked down in rural Serbia in 2011 and put on trial in the Dutch city.

The sentence for the man known as the "Butcher of Bosnia" was upheld on appeal by the UN court in 2021. He was being given palliative care in the hospital of the UN detention facility, where he died.

In a statement confirming the death on Thursday, the UN Court said Dutch authorities have begun an investigation.

It added that the court's top judge"has ordered a full inquiry into the circumstances" of Mladić's death.

In May, the court rejected a bid for his release from jail as he was nearing the end of his life.

The judge agreed his situation was "dire" but ruled that he was receiving "comprehensive and compassionate treatment" in prison.

Mladić's lawyers said at the time that he had already been bedbound or in a wheelchair for a long time and later had suffered a suspected stroke that left him almost unable to speak.

Mladić - who never recognised the UN court - had been held at The Hague detention facility since 2011.

He commanded Bosnian Serb forces in the 1990s against the Bosnian Croat and Bosniak (Bosnian Muslim) armies.

During the war his troops committed what became known as "ethnic cleansing" in Bosnia-Herzegovina in a bid to expel the non-Serbian population by force. They besieged the main city of Sarajevo with the deaths of more than 10,000 people, and carried out the massacre of 8,000 men and boys at Srebrenica.

Hasan Hasanović , a Srebrenica survivor who lost his twin brother and father in the massacre, told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme that Mladić's death "does not bring closure because the people who were killed in Srebrenica cannot come back".

"His death is just a biological necessity, and it doesn't bring to an end the political project and military project that created that legacy of genocide. And we now live with the consequences of a divided country, genocide denial," said Hasanović, who now works at the Srebrenica memorial centre.

However, Bosnian Serb separatist leader Milorad Dodik told Reuters news agency that Mladić "was respected by Serbian people. As a commander he stood to defend Serbs."

"I genuinely believe he protected the Serbian people, because after all, that was his duty," a man called Milan was quoted as saying by Reuters.

Another man, Vasilije, said: "It's a massive shame, it really is. Personally, I think it's a total injustice that he was even thrown in The Hague."
body.zh: 被定罪的波斯尼亚塞族战犯拉特科·姆拉迪奇在海牙联合国监狱内死亡，享年 84 岁。 2017年，他因在1992-95年前南斯拉夫战争期间犯下种族灭绝罪、战争罪和反人类罪而被判终身监禁。 波斯尼亚战争结束后，他逃亡了 16 年，直到 2011 年终于在塞尔维亚农村被抓获，并在荷兰城市接受审判。 2021年，联合国法院在上诉中维持了对这位被称为“波斯尼亚屠夫”的男子的判决。他当时在联合国拘留设施的医院接受姑息治疗，并在那里去世。 联合国法院在周四确认死亡的声明中表示，荷兰当局已开始调查。 它补充说，法院最高法官“已下令对姆拉迪奇的死亡情况进行全面调查”。 五月，法院驳回了他的出狱请求，因为他已接近生命的尽头。 法官承认他的处境“严峻”，但裁定他在监狱中接受“全面和富有同情心的治疗”。 姆拉迪奇的律师当时表示，他已经长期卧床或坐在轮椅上，后来疑似中风，导致他几乎无法说话。 姆拉迪奇从未承认联合国法院，自 2011 年以来一直被关押在海牙拘留所。 20世纪90年代，他指挥波斯尼亚塞族军队对抗波斯尼亚克族和波斯尼亚克族（波斯尼亚穆斯林）军队。 战争期间，他的军队在波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那实施了所谓的“种族清洗”，以武力驱逐非塞尔维亚人口。他们包围了主要城市萨拉热窝，造成一万多人死亡，并在斯雷布雷尼察屠杀了八千名男子和男孩。 斯雷布雷尼察幸存者哈桑·哈萨诺维奇在大屠杀中失去了双胞胎兄弟和父亲，他告诉英国广播公司世界频道的新闻小时节目，姆拉迪奇的死“并没有结束，因为在斯雷布雷尼察遇难的人无法回来”。 现在在斯雷布雷尼察纪念中心工作的哈萨诺维奇说：“他的死只是生理上的必然，它并不会结束造成种族灭绝遗产的政治计划和军事计划。我们现在生活在一个分裂的国家和否认种族灭绝的后果中。” 然而，波斯尼亚塞族分离主义领导人米洛拉德·多迪克告诉路透社，姆拉迪奇“受到塞尔维亚人民的尊重。作为一名指挥官，他致力于保卫塞尔维亚人。” 路透社援引一位名叫米兰的男子的话说：“我真诚地相信他保护了塞尔维亚人民，因为毕竟这是他的职责。” 另一名男子瓦西里耶说：“这确实是一个巨大的耻辱。就我个人而言，我认为他被扔到海牙是完全不公正的。”

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Zambian opposition leader in police custody: state media
title.zh: 赞比亚反对派领导人被警方拘留：官方媒体

summary.en: Zambia's national broadcaster reports that Brian Mundubile, who wanted to challenge this month's presidential election results, and his running mate have surrendered to police and are being interviewed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 赞比亚国家广播公司报道称，想要挑战本月总统选举结果的布赖恩·蒙杜比莱(Brian Mundubile)和他的竞选搭档已向警方自首并正在接受采访。 据国家广播公司 ZNBC 周四报道，赞比亚反对派领导人、总统选举亚军布赖恩·蒙杜比莱 (Brian Mundubile) 已被警方拘留并接受讯问。 这是在一场有争议但基本和平的总统选举两周后发生的，当局宣布现任总统哈凯恩德·希奇莱马获胜。 选举第二天，蒙杜比莱在警方突击搜查和逮捕后一直躲藏起来，称他计划在法庭上质疑选举结果，因为政府指控他犯有国家安全罪并密谋叛乱。 国家广播公司 ZNBC 报道称，蒙杜比莱和他的竞选搭档马克比·祖鲁“已被移交给警方，目前正在接受采访”。 警方发言人戈弗雷·奇拉比 (Godfrey Chilabi) 表示，两名反对派领导人正在接受执法人员的询问，他们的律师也在场。 奇拉比告诉 ZNBC，采访过程结束后将发表一份声明。 该广播公司报道称，两人在向警方自首之前一直在首都卢萨卡“受到联合国的保护”。 警方还表示，蒙杜比莱本周早些时候正在向一个“国际组织”寻求庇护，并表示该组织正在对反对派候选人及其竞选伙伴进行询问，试图在他们与“各种令人震惊的活动……有可能威胁或破坏国家安全”之间建立联系。 赞比亚于 8 月 13 日进行了投票，观察人士原本预计这次选举将为现任总统哈凯恩德·希奇莱马 (Hakainde Hichilema) 的第二个任期提供相对明确的授权。 蒙杜比莱在选举之夜短暂宣布获胜，但希奇莱马呼吁人们等待计票和正式结果。 由于据称针对选举官员的袭击，计票过程一度短暂暂停。选举委员会最终发现希奇莱马赢得了约 60% 的选票，尽管蒙杜比莱的表现好于预期。 希奇莱马在投票前不久指控威胁国家安全的阴谋，投票后第二天，警方突袭了蒙杜比莱的家和其他反对派地点，逮捕了 11 人。前内阁部长穆托维·卡夫瓦亚 (Mutotwe Kafwaya) 在行动中的交火中被枪杀。蒙杜比勒躲了起来。 在希奇莱马之前统治赞比亚的团结与繁荣民族和解党 (NRPUP) 的领导人...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

title.en: Nepal flooding: 'We are disconnected from Kathmandu'
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水：“我们与加德满都失去联系”

summary.en: DW spoke with people from the Nepali regions devastated by flash floods about the fates of their family members, with a government minister warning that the state was not ready for a disaster of such magnitude.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
DW spoke with people from the Nepali regions devastated by flash floods about the fates of their family members, with a government minister warning that the state was not ready for a disaster of such magnitude.

With the death toll in Nepal well into the hundreds and rising following a massive flash flood on Wednesday , the full scope of destruction remains unclear. 

People from the affected areas told DW that many villages remain both physically and electronically cut off from the capital, Kathmandu.

Bidhya Rajput, a journalist based in the capital, said her home in the Sole village in Nepal 's Nuwakot District was swept away by the Trisuli River.

"As far as we know, only four or five people from Sole village could save their lives by fleeing towards the hills. Others couldn't make their way as the floods came up suddenly," she told DW.

The government has declared Nuwakot, along with Rasuwa and Dhading districts, to be the most affected by the deadly floods.

Rajput told DW her husband's parents remain missing. Her father-in-law, a teacher, may have been caught in the flood while returning home after work, according to the school principal.

Rajput's husband has left for the village in search for news on his family members, despite the roads being damaged and swept away in many places. Rajput said that there are no further updates from the village as there has been no electricity or mobile communication since early morning on Thursday.

"The state's rescue and relief efforts have been centered mostly on bigger cities," she said, adding that "state assistance is yet to reach Sole." 

Villagers said the same area was  affected by flooding last year , but many villagers managed to get to higher ground and the water did not reach as high as on Tuesday.

"Had the villagers received early warning information, [and] could have presumed that this time floods would be so massive, they could have fled to safe locations like last year," Rajput said. "This time, they couldn't get even that chance."

But Usha Kiran Timsena, an opposition politician from Nuwakot, said police and local officials did issue a warning that a massive flood was coming. However, many people in the area simply didn't account for the scale and speed of the mass of water. 

"Many those who were a bit far from riversides took it lightly and couldn't flee once the flood reaches to their places," she told DW.

"Two of my close relatives have been missing since yesterday morning. There has been no further update or contact since then."

Authorities said that more than three dozen bridges, including vehicular and suspension bridges, as well as a dozen hydropower dams, have been destroyed by the floods.

body.zh: 德国之声采访了遭受山洪袭击的尼泊尔地区的人们，讲述了他们家人的命运，一位政府部长警告说，该国还没有准备好应对如此严重的灾难。 尼泊尔周三发生大规模山洪，死亡人数已达数百人，且死亡人数不断上升，破坏的全部范围仍不清楚。 来自受影响地区的人们告诉德国之声，许多村庄仍然与首都加德满都在物理上和电子上隔绝。 首都记者比迪亚·拉杰普特 (Bidhya Rajput) 表示，她位于尼泊尔努瓦科特区索尔村的家被特里苏里河冲走了。 她告诉德国之声：“据我们所知，索尔村只有四五个人逃到山上才能保住性命。洪水突然袭来，其他人都无法逃生。” 政府宣布努瓦科特以及拉苏瓦和达丁地区是受致命洪水影响最严重的地区。 拉杰普特告诉德国之声，她丈夫的父母仍然失踪。据学校校长称，她的岳父是一名教师，可能在下班回家时被洪水淹没。 尽管许多地方的道路都被损坏和冲毁，拉吉普特的丈夫还是前往村庄寻找家人的消息。拉杰普特表示，该村没有进一步的更新消息，因为自周四凌晨以来就没有电力或移动通讯。 “该州的救援工作主要集中在大城市，”她说，并补充说“国家援助尚未到达索尔。” 村民们表示，去年同一地区曾遭受洪水影响，但许多村民设法到达地势较高的地方，水位没有像周二那么高。 拉吉普特说：“如果村民收到早期预警信息，他们可能会推测这次洪水会如此之大，他们可能会像去年一样逃到安全的地方。” “这一次，他们连这个机会都没有了。” 但努瓦科特的反对派政治家乌沙·基兰·蒂姆塞纳表示，警方和当地官员确实发出了大规模洪水即将到来的警告。然而，该地区的许多人根本没有考虑到水团的规模和速度。 她告诉德国之声：“许多距离河边稍远的人对此掉以轻心，一旦洪水到达他们所在的地方，他们就无法逃离。” “我的两名近亲从昨天早上起就失踪了。此后就没有进一步的更新或联系。” 当局表示，超过三打桥梁，包括行车桥和吊桥，以及十几座水电站大坝，已被洪水摧毁。 来自 Dhading 的苏扬·洛哈尼 (Sujan Lohani) 告诉德国之声，他从未...

title.en: Ex-Bosnian Serb military leader Ratko Mladic dead at 84
title.zh: 前波斯尼亚塞族军事领导人拉特科·姆拉迪奇去世，享年84岁

summary.en: The former Bosnian Serb general was convicted of genocide committed during the bloody 1992-95 war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
summary.zh: 这位前波斯尼亚塞族将军因在1992-95年血腥的波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那战争期间犯下种族灭绝罪而被定罪。

body.en:
The former Bosnian Serb general was convicted of genocide committed during the bloody 1992-95 war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Bosnian Serb general Ratko Mladic, who was serving a life sentence for war crimes committed during  Bosnia and Herzegovina's 1992-95 war has died, a United Nations official said. 

Serbian state broadcaster RTS reported on Thursday that he died in a prison hospital in the Hague, after suffering several strokes.

A family member of Mladic, who spoke on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity of the situation, confirmed the reports to the Associated Press and said Mladic's son, Darko Mladic, was on the way to the Hague.

The International Criminal Court for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) convicted Mladic of charges including crimes against humanity and genocide in 2017, handing him a life sentence. The  verdict was confirmed on appeal in 2021.

Commenting on Mladic's death on Thursday, United Nations Secretary General Antonio Guterres expressed his support for the war criminal's victims.

"The secretary-general stands in solidarity with the victims, survivors and their families who suffered the crimes for which Mr Mladic was found guilty," spokesman Stephane Dujarric told reporters.   

Mladic was held responsible for his role in the 1992 to 1995 war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including July 1995 massacre of some 8,000 Muslim men and boys at Srebrenica.

The slaughter, the worst single atrocity in Europe since World War II, saw him named the  "Butcher of Bosnia."

Under Mladic's command, Bosnian Serb forces besieged Sarajevo and other towns, operated detention camps for non-Serbs and enemy soldiers, and systematically killed prisoners.

Former UN rights chief Zeid Ra'ad al Hussein described him as "the epitome of evil" after his conviction.

"This is all lies, you are all liars," he shouted when he was sentenced to life in prison in 2017.

On Monday, Serbia's justice minister, Nenad Vujic, asked for Mladic to be transferred to a Belgrade military hospital, warning that his death "could come at any time."

Born in Bosnia in 1942, Mladic was a former Yugoslav army officer who rose to command the Bosnian Serb army during the 1992-95 war.

A hardline nationalist, he portrayed the conflict as a historic struggle against Ottoman rule and celebrated the 1995 capture of Srebrenica.

After the capture of the city, Mladic ordered the evacuation of women, children and the elderly but said all men of fighting age are taken prisoner.

In the following days more than 8,000 Muslim men and boys are systematically butchered by the Bosnian Serb forces and their bodies dumped in mass graves.

body.zh: 这位前波斯尼亚塞族将军被判犯有 1992-95 年波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那血腥战争期间犯下的种族灭绝罪。 一名联合国官员表示，因在 1992-95 年波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那战争期间犯下战争罪而被判无期徒刑的波斯尼亚塞族将军拉特科·姆拉迪奇已经死亡。 塞尔维亚国家广播公司 RTS 周四报道称，他多次中风，在海牙的一家监狱医院去世。 姆拉迪奇的一名家庭成员因情况敏感而不愿透露姓名，他向美联社证实了这一报道，并表示姆拉迪奇的儿子达科·姆拉迪奇正在前往海牙的途中。 2017年，前南斯拉夫国际刑事法院（ICTY）判定姆拉迪奇犯有反人类罪和种族灭绝罪，判处他无期徒刑。 该判决于 2021 年上诉后得到确认。 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯周四在评论姆拉迪奇之死时表达了对战犯受害者的支持。 发言人斯蒂芬·杜雅里克对记者表示：“秘书长对姆拉迪奇先生被判有罪的罪行的受害者、幸存者及其家人表示声援。” 姆拉迪奇被指控在 1992 年至 1995 年波斯尼亚和黑塞哥维那战争中所扮演的角色，包括 1995 年 7 月在斯雷布雷尼察屠杀约 8,000 名穆斯林男子和男孩。 这次屠杀是二战以来欧洲最严重的一次暴行，他被称为“波斯尼亚屠夫”。 在姆拉迪奇的指挥下，波斯尼亚塞族军队包围了萨拉热窝和其他城镇，为非塞族人和敌方士兵设立了拘留营，并有系统地杀害囚犯。 前联合国人权事务高级专员扎伊德·拉阿德·侯赛因在被定罪后称他为“邪恶的缩影”。 “这都是谎言，你们都是骗子，”2017年被判处终身监禁时他喊道。 周一，塞尔维亚司法部长内纳德·胡伊奇 (Nenad Vujic) 要求将姆拉迪奇转移到贝尔格莱德军事医院，并警告说他的死亡“随时可能发生”。 姆拉迪奇 1942 年出生于波斯尼亚，是一名前南斯拉夫军官，在 1992-95 战争期间升任波斯尼亚塞族军队指挥。 作为一名强硬民族主义者，他将这场冲突描述为一场反对奥斯曼帝国统治的历史性斗争，并庆祝 1995 年攻占斯雷布雷尼察。 占领这座城市后，姆拉迪奇下令疏散妇女、儿童和老人，但表示所有战斗年龄的男子都被俘虏。 在接下来的几天里，超过 8,000 名穆斯林男子和男孩被波斯尼亚塞族军队系统地屠杀，他们的尸体被扔进万人坑。 2022 年，荷兰为荷兰维和人员的行为道歉...

Yahweh's word in Hebrews 9:27 speaks to a universal truth: every life, regardless of earthly power or conviction, will ultimately face death and a divine judgment. While earthly courts strive for...
reflection.zh: 拉特科·姆拉迪奇在波斯尼亚战争期间因种族灭绝罪被定罪后，于84岁去世的消息，提醒我们人类对公义的深切渴望。雅伟在希伯来书9:27中的话语揭示了一个普世真理：无论世俗权力或判决如何，每个人终将面对死亡和随之而来的神圣审判。尽管世俗法庭努力追究责任，但这节经文指向一个超越人类系统的最终审判，为所有行为的最终后果提供了一个严肃的视角。

verse.textEn: Just as people are destined to die once, and after that to face judgment.
verse.textZh: 按着定命，人人都有一死，死后且有审判。

title.en: Could new US sanctions tear China and Iran apart?
title.zh: 美国新制裁是否会导致中国和伊朗分裂？

summary.en: Washington's strategy of putting maximum economic pressure on Iran is tempered by its desire to smooth political tensions with China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Washington's strategy of putting maximum economic pressure on Iran is tempered by its desire to smooth political tensions with China.

China has pushed back on what it called "illegal unilateral sanctions" after the US announced new measures earlier this week to cut off all potential sources of revenue to Iran.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday described the sanctions package as an "economic D-Day" against Tehran, and warned any economic engagement with the regime would "expose those responsible to the full reach" of US power.

China is Iran's top trade partner and provides a lifeline to Tehran mainly through oil purchases , but also with banking, technology and dual-use goods, which can be used both for civilian and military purposes.

When asked whether Chinese banks would be included in the new measures, Bessent warned that "no one was above the reach of US sanctions."

But with US President Donald Trump due to meet his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in September, Washington will need to be careful with any moves affecting China-Iran trade ties.

The initial US sanctions package stops short of targeting major Chinese banks. Instead, it focuses on 60 smaller entities, individuals, and vessels, both in mainland China and Hong Kong, that are part of the ecosystem supporting "illicit nuclear and missile technology procurement, cyber operations, and oil‑revenue generation networks."

China purchases up to 90% of Iranian oil exports, some of it through independent "teapot" refineries which end up rebranding the oil or using intermediaries to bypass US sanctions.

In May, China's Commerce Ministry ordered domestic businesses and teapot refineries to ignore US restrictions targeting several of these refineries. At the time, Bessent said China's Iran oil purchases amounted to "funding the largest state sponsor of terrorism."

On Tuesday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said cooperation between China and Iran "has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be interfered with or disrupted."

China maintains a transactional relationship while framing instability in the Middle East as a failure of US policy . At the same time, Beijing also projects the image of a stable, responsible superpower , and avoids being lumped together with rogue states the US accuses it of supporting. Beijing also values its trade ties with Saudi Arabia and the UAE, prompting it to carefully balance its relationships to avoid alienating Iran's regional rivals.

The ongoing conflict in the Middle East and the US sanctions package are likely to be on the agenda when Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian attends the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO)...

title.en: 'Massive attack': Russia is intensifying its strikes on Ukraine
title.zh: “大规模袭击”：俄罗斯正在加强对乌克兰的打击

summary.en: Russia's attacks on key targets follow an uptick in the country's attack on Ukraine.

body.en:
Russia hammered the Ukrainian capital Kyiv and other cities with missiles and drones early on Thursday, officials said, targeting warehouses, ports, and energy and industrial facilities in an hours-long assault that dragged into the morning.

Commuters in Kyiv streamed to work under the booming sound of air defences firing at jet-powered drones attacking the city in several waves, after an overnight barrage that included an unspecified number of ballistic missiles and 258 drones.

"Overnight, Russia carried out a massive strike against Ukraine, targeting ports, grain storage, energy, industry, and other infrastructure with ballistic and hypersonic missiles and combat drones," Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on X.

Russia has stepped up its air war on Ukraine in recent months, pummelling its cities with larger numbers of ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones amid a critical shortage of air defences.

President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said this week Ukraine had recently received a small batch of the US-made Patriot interceptors capable of downing the fast-moving ballistic missiles, which are notoriously difficult to intercept.

In a statement on Thursday, Kyiv's air force said Ukrainian forces had downed seven ballistic missiles, one anti-ship cruise missile, and nearly 90 per cent of the drones.

One person was killed and two more injured in a lunchtime attack on a shopping centre in Ukraine's second-biggest city of Kharkiv, said regional governor Oleh Syniehubov.

In Kyiv, debris fell in at least two districts, damaging a school and shattering windows at a healthcare facility, said Mayor Vitali Klitschko. Two people were injured in a daytime attack, he added.

Two people were wounded outside the capital after strikes damaged warehouses and private homes, the regional governor said. Reuters TV footage showed a big plume of smoke over a warehouse in the region.

In the central Poltava region, air attacks targeted industrial sites and an energy facility, cutting power to seven settlements, its regional governor said.

In Zelenskiy's hometown of Kryvyi Rih, a steel-and-mining hub, three people were wounded after a missile strike on an industrial facility there, said governor Oleksandr Hanzha.

Three more people were wounded in the southern city of Zaporizhzhia after strikes on an unspecified production facility, according to regional chief Ivan Fedorov.

In an hours-long attack on the southern Odesa region, infrastructure, an educational facility and a multi-storey building were damaged, officials said. Three people were wounded.

title.en: What led 35 Australians to the remote Nepal valley hit by deadly floods?
title.zh: 是什么原因导致35名澳大利亚人来到尼泊尔偏远山谷，并遭遇致命洪水？

summary.en: Dozens of Australians are among hundreds of tourists missing after deadly floods and landslides struck Nepal's remote Langtang Valley, a popular trekking destination. Rescuers are battling difficult terrain and lack of infrastructure in their search efforts.
summary.zh: 尼泊尔偏远的朗塘谷地（一个热门徒步目的地）遭遇致命洪水和山体滑坡后，数十名澳大利亚人与数百名游客失踪。救援人员正在崎岖地形和基础设施缺乏的条件下努力搜寻。

body.en:
At least 35 Australians are missing after a flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border, with many caught up in one of Nepal's most popular trekking regions, the remote Langtang Valley.

Some 644 tourists — 517 of them foreigners — were unaccounted for several hours after the disaster struck on Wednesday , according to Nepal's tourism ministry. Chinese rescuers are searching for hundreds more in Tibet.

It's feared many more are missing or dead, as rescuers battle a lack of infrastructure and remote, mountainous terrain to search through mud and debris.

Foreign Minister Penny Wong spoke about why so many foreign nationals were in the area in a press conference on Thursday afternoon.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"It is well–known that this area, people are not only going there for trekking but also for spiritual reasons, so you would anticipate that the foreign nationals who were in the region would have been there for a variety of reasons," Wong said.

She said it may take time for the Australian government and Nepalese authorities to understand how many people are missing or dead.

"I can only outline the numbers we are aware of today," Wong said. "The numbers of foreign nationals are higher and as yet we do not have any further information about if there are any more of those who are Australian.

"We will continue to try to ascertain if there are any Australians who are not accounted for over and above the 34 that we are aware of."

United States-based tourist company Himalayan Glacier confirmed 15 Australians who were on one of its tours are missing and unaccounted for in the Langtang Valley.

The company's chief executive said he had not been able to contact the group of 47 people — which includes 15 Australians, nine Nepalese, two from the United Kingdom, two from Singapore and others from the US and Russia, the ABC has reported.

Among the Australians missing are nine men and six women. The youngest are boys aged 14 and 11, and the oldest is a woman aged 64.

The flood hit Syabrubesi, is the starting point for the popular Langtang trek, as well as other areas used by travellers for Hindu pilgrimage to Kailash Mansarovar.

It's not the standard Mount Everest trekking route, but the valley it leads to — Langtang Valley — is the third most popular trekking area in Nepal, just behind Everest and the Annapurna region.

Langtang is a narrow valley running north from the Syabrubesi gateway, hemmed in by snow-capped peaks — including mountain Langtang Lirung, which stands over 7,000m tall — with icy landscapes, rivers and glaciers lining the route.

title.en: 'Creative thinking is born of loneliness': Artist Yayoi Kusama dies at 97
title.zh: “创造性思维源于孤独”：艺术家草间弥生去世，享年 97 岁

summary.en: Japan's "polka dot queen" has been remembered for her remarkable originality.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The dotty pumpkins and kaleidoscope rooms of Yayoi Kusama, who has died aged 97, were as vibrant as the artist herself, but her exuberant work was the expression of a long battle with mental illness.

Once a fixture of the 1960s pop and minimalist scenes in New York, Japan's "polka dot queen" found huge commercial success in her later decades.

Her larger-than-life paintings, sculptures and installations — inspired by vivid hallucinations — sold for millions of dollars and packed out top galleries.

Kusama, instantly recognisable in her bright red wig and bold spotted outfits, worked well into old age from the psychiatric hospital in Tokyo where she lived voluntarily for the second half of her life.

But she also struggled with her feelings for her home country, which she left for decades and once described as "full of disdain for women".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Born in 1929, the youngest daughter of a wealthy but troubled family, Kusama started producing her signature dot and net patterns at the age of 10.

"My mother had regrets about my birth, and I was driven to the edge psychologically," she wrote in her autobiography, A Personal History of Polka Dots.

"One day, after seeing a tablecloth with a red flower pattern on a desk, I saw the same red flower pattern all over the ceiling, windows and pillars. It filled the room, and covered my body."

Art provided a release for the young Kusama, whose father, a seedling merchant, was unfaithful to her mother.

"When I was sad or lonely, everything would be cured when I drew pictures," she said.

In the book, Kusama explained her concept of "self-obliteration" — a recurrent theme throughout her career.

"I put dots all over my body and make all the surroundings dot patterns. By creating the same thing over and over, my own existence is buried in the art."

Kusama studied Japanese painting in Kyoto, against her parents' wishes, and held her first solo exhibition in 1952 in her hometown of Matsumoto in central Japan.

At the show, she met a psychiatrist who advised her to go and work abroad — an idea that appealed to her.

"Japan was so small, vulgar, feudalistic and full of disdain for women," said the artist.

"I was born and raised in Japan, but I'm not influenced by Japanese culture and tradition."

The decisive push to pack her bags came when she wrote to modernist painter Georgia O'Keeffe, who encouraged Kusama to seek international recognition in the United States.

Kusama moved to Seattle in 1957 and then to New York, where she struggled to find her place as an Asian artist in the city's largely white, male-dominated creative scene.

title.en: A landmark US deal could change social media forever

summary.en: Meta Platforms has agreed to pay up to $25 billion over the next decade to settle lawsuits from nearly all 50 US states alleging that Facebook and Instagram were designed to addict children. The deal includes strict new limits on how teenagers interact with these platforms to address concerns over mental health and...
summary.zh: Meta公司已同意在未来十年内支付高达250亿美元，以解决美国近50个州发起的诉讼。这些州指控Facebook和Instagram的设计旨在让儿童成瘾。该协议还包括对青少年使用这些平台的严格新限制，以应对对其心理健康和安全的担忧。

body.en:
Meta Platforms will pay up to US$18 billion ($25 billion) over the next decade and strictly limit how teenagers use Facebook and Instagram under an agreement with nearly all 50 US states that took it to trial to resolve claims it designed those social media platforms to addict children.

The settlements announced on Wednesday end a federal trial over allegations Meta's products harmed children, and the company misled the public about their safety. Four of the states — California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey — were expected to seek close to US$200 billion ($279 billion) in civil penalties.

While Meta will not undergo a fundamental overhaul, the accords represent a sweeping effort to define how it serves young users.

It could provide a template for resolving thousands of other lawsuits against social media companies. Governments around the world are trying to curb children's access to harmful online content, including a ban in Australia on social media for children under 16.

“The focus of this case was to protect our kids," Colorado Attorney General Phil Weiser said in a statement. "The relief we are getting in this settlement is very meaningful and well beyond what any court has ordered or is likely to order."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Meta agreed over the next decade to restrict teenagers' use of Facebook and Instagram to two hours a day and block all usage from midnight to 6am, absent parental consent.

These limits could be tightened if the social media platforms Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube adopt similar terms. Meta will also disable most push notifications to teenage users during school hours of 8am to 3pm and enhance measures to prevent children from accessing age-restricted content.

The settlement does not require Meta to abandon personalised recommendations or targeted advertising. It also does not address some content Meta researchers found particularly problematic, including posts that made Instagram users uncomfortable with their body image.

Meta denied wrongdoing in agreeing to settle. The total payout represents about three to four months of profit and about one month of revenue for Meta.

"Ensuring teens have a safe and productive experience on our platforms is an absolute imperative for Meta," the Menlo Park, California-based company said in a blog post. "We want to get this right for parents and teens."

Meta agreed to make maximum payments of about US$16.7 billion ($22 billion) to 47 U.S. states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands.

title.en: Could new US sanctions tear China and Iran apart?
title.zh: 美国新制裁是否会导致中国和伊朗分裂？

summary.en: Washington's strategy of putting maximum economic pressure on Iran is tempered by its desire to smooth political tensions with China.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Washington's strategy of putting maximum economic pressure on Iran is tempered by its desire to smooth political tensions with China.

China has pushed back on what it called "illegal unilateral sanctions" after the US announced new measures earlier this week to cut off all potential sources of revenue to Iran.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday described the sanctions package as an "economic D-Day" against Tehran, and warned any economic engagement with the regime would "expose those responsible to the full reach" of US power.

China is Iran's top trade partner and provides a lifeline to Tehran mainly through oil purchases , but also with banking, technology and dual-use goods, which can be used both for civilian and military purposes.

When asked whether Chinese banks would be included in the new measures, Bessent warned that "no one was above the reach of US sanctions."

But with US President Donald Trump due to meet his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in September, Washington will need to be careful with any moves affecting China-Iran trade ties.

The initial US sanctions package stops short of targeting major Chinese banks. Instead, it focuses on 60 smaller entities, individuals, and vessels, both in mainland China and Hong Kong, that are part of the ecosystem supporting "illicit nuclear and missile technology procurement, cyber operations, and oil‑revenue generation networks."

China purchases up to 90% of Iranian oil exports, some of it through independent "teapot" refineries which end up rebranding the oil or using intermediaries to bypass US sanctions.

In May, China's Commerce Ministry ordered domestic businesses and teapot refineries to ignore US restrictions targeting several of these refineries. At the time, Bessent said China's Iran oil purchases amounted to "funding the largest state sponsor of terrorism."

On Tuesday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said cooperation between China and Iran "has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be interfered with or disrupted."

China maintains a transactional relationship while framing instability in the Middle East as a failure of US policy . At the same time, Beijing also projects the image of a stable, responsible superpower , and avoids being lumped together with rogue states the US accuses it of supporting. Beijing also values its trade ties with Saudi Arabia and the UAE, prompting it to carefully balance its relationships to avoid alienating Iran's regional rivals.

The ongoing conflict in the Middle East and the US sanctions package are likely to be on the agenda when Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian attends the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO)...
body.zh: 华盛顿对伊朗施加最大经济压力的战略因其缓和与中国政治紧张局势的愿望而受到影响。 在美国本周早些时候宣布切断伊朗所有潜在收入来源的新措施后，中国反击了所谓的“非法单边制裁”。 美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特周一将制裁计划描述为针对德黑兰的“经济诺曼底登陆”，并警告称，与该政权的任何经济接触都将“让责任人暴露在美国力量的全面影响之下”。 中国是伊朗最大的贸易伙伴，主要通过购买石油为德黑兰提供生命线，但也提供银行、技术和军民两用商品，这些商品可用于民用和军事目的。 当被问及中资银行是否会被纳入新措施时，贝森特警告称，“没有一家银行能够逃脱美国的制裁”。 但由于美国总统唐纳德·特朗普将于 9 月会见中国国家主席习近平，华盛顿需要谨慎对待任何影响中伊贸易关系的举动。 美国最初的制裁方案并未针对中国主要银行。相反，它重点关注中国大陆和香港的 60 个较小的实体、个人和船只，这些实体、个人和船只是支持“非法核和导弹技术采购、网络运营和石油创收网络”的生态系统的一部分。 中国购买伊朗出口石油的90%，其中一些是通过独立的“茶壶”炼油厂购买的，这些炼油厂最终重塑石油品牌或利用中间商绕过美国的制裁。 五月，中国商务部命令国内企业和茶壶炼油厂无视美国针对其中几家炼油厂的限制。当时，贝森特表示，中国购买伊朗石油相当于“为恐怖主义最大的国家资助者提供资金”。 周二，中国外交部发言人林健表示，中伊合作“始终在国际法框架内进行，不应受到干扰和破坏”。 中国维持着交易关系，同时将中东的不稳定视为美国政策的失败。与此同时，北京还塑造了一个稳定、负责任的超级大国的形象，避免与美国指责其支持的流氓国家混为一谈。北京还重视与沙特阿拉伯和阿联酋的贸易关系，促使其谨慎平衡关系，以避免疏远伊朗的地区竞争对手。 当伊朗总统马苏德·佩泽什基安出席上海合作组织（SCO）时，中东持续的冲突和美国的制裁方案可能会被列入议程......

title.en: What caused the Nepal-Tibet flash floods?
title.zh: 尼泊尔西藏山洪爆发的原因是什么？

summary.en: At least 270 people have died in the massive flash floods, while more than 800 others are missing.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US Geological Survey says the floods in the Nepal-Tibet border were triggered by a "glacial collapse" - meaning a glacier or part of a glacier had disintegrated.

Initial reports led authorities to believe that an earthquake had been the cause.

The cause of the glacial collapse has not been determined, but scientists have warned that Himalayan glaciers are melting at an accelerating rate due to rising temperatures and climate change.
body.zh: 美国地质调查局表示，尼泊尔和西藏边境的洪水是由“冰川崩塌”引发的，这意味着冰川或部分冰川崩解。 初步报告使当局相信地震是造成事故的原因。 冰川崩塌的原因尚未确定，但科学家警告说，由于气温上升和气候变化，喜马拉雅冰川正在加速融化。

title.en: What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
title.zh: 我们对尼泊尔和西藏致命洪水的了解

summary.en: Hundreds have died in flooding and landslides on the border of Nepal and Tibet.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Massive landslides and flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have caused widespread damage and left hundreds dead or missing.

Search and rescue operations are under way. Chinese state media has said there are significant casualties, while Nepalese officials anticipate "huge scale loss".

Nepal's foreign minister initially said an earthquake was reported on the Tibet-Nepal border shortly before the landslide, suggesting it may have triggered the disaster.

The United States Geological Survey (USGS) had first reported the event as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake on Wednesday, but later confirmed the incident "was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow" that "caused subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream".

"Additional analysis of nearby seismic stations, long period seismic waves, and satellite imagery led to the determination that the seismic event was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow, and that no earthquake had occurred," USGS said on Thursday.

Earlier Nepali authorities had also told the BBC that a massive chunk of ice may have collapsed from a mountain, pulling down rocks and other sediments with it.

Climate change is known to be driving faster glacier melt in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region and, as rescue efforts continue, scientists are trying to piece together the exact order of events.

Simon Cook, senior lecturer in energy environment and security at the University of Dundee who specialises in glaciology, said "climate change could have an impact".

Cook said his team had detected that the lower part of a glacier in Nepal near the Langtang Lirung peak - which is approximately 15km (9 miles) west of the site of the floods - had collapsed.

He estimated that the glacier collapsed in a northwesterly direction and then travelled westwards downstream.

He told the BBC "permafrost is partially holding some mountainsides together, this permafrost is warming and thawing and degrading so you are going to get more landslides".

Mike Searle, professor of Earth sciences at Oxford University, said the glacier could have collapsed "hours or days" before the flooding hit Nepal and Tibet.

He told the BBC: "I think the sheer wave of debris suggests there was a landslide first, the water built up, (which) dammed the river, and then it burst in one huge great flood."

One possibility is that water from rainfall or melting ice may have destabilised the ground or ice, triggering a chain reaction.

Scientist will be looking at satellite images of exactly where the landslide occurred, whether any glacial lakes suddenly drained, and where the river might have become blocked, as well as data on recent rainfall.

title.en: Nepal floods: Hundreds killed, over 1,000 missing
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水：数百人死亡、逾千人失踪

summary.en: Rescue teams are searching for survivors after a glacial collapse triggered catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet. Hundreds of people, including many foreign tourists, are missing.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Rescue teams are searching for survivors after a glacial collapse triggered catastrophic floods in Nepal and Tibet. Hundreds of people, including many foreign tourists, are missing.

The death toll from catastrophic flash floods along the border between  Nepal  and Tibet has risen to at least 392, while more than 1,400 people were missing.

Rescue teams were searching for survivors on Thursday, a day after a glacial collapse sent a huge wall of mud and rock barreling through the Himalayan communities, sweeping away entire villages.

Even with rescue efforts underway, local authorities warned that a fresh disaster could occur as a lake that had formed due to the floodwaters was threatening to burst.

In Tibet, Chinese broadcaster CCTV reported 558 people missing in Gyirong county, including 260 foreigners. Three deaths had been confirmed there as of Thursday morning, with two villagers rescued.

The disaster struck Wednesday when a glacial collapse triggered a flood in the Lhende Khola river, a tributary of the Bhotekoshi, in a corridor popular with trekkers and pilgrims connecting Kathmandu with Lhasa. 

Nepal police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle told Reuters the death toll "will go up, as we have resumed the search and more bodies are expected to be recovered."

Neighboring India accounts for the largest proportion of missing foreign nationals. Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar said that 288 Indians were unaccounted for in Nepal, while a further 200 were stranded in China awaiting rescue.

US officials said around 90 US citizens remained unaccounted for on Thursday. The US State Department said three have been rescued, but that it was not yet aware of any deaths among US citizens.

Sunil Sharma, a Nepal tourism board spokesperson, told the AP news agency that many of the missing were pilgrims traveling to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a site sacred to Hindus. In addition to the Indian and US tourists, Sharma said 34 Australians, 33 Britons and 24 Canadians were also missing.

Reuters cited other police and tourism officials who put the missing tourists at 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada.

China's Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were unaccounted for. 

During a press conference in Beijing, foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said they were still verifying the breakdown of nationalities of the missing foreigners in Tibet, who were mostly tourists and pilgrims.

China authorities said they were in close communication ‌with Nepal on search and rescue efforts.

Chinese premier Li Qiang has traveled to affected areas in Tibet to view the emergency work, state media reported.

title.en: Number of Australians missing in Nepal floods climbs to 35
title.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪，其中包括澳大利亚人

summary.en: Aid workers have described scenes of complete destruction, with entire settlements "wiped out".
summary.zh: 救援人员描述了彻底毁灭的景象，整个定居点“被夷为平地”。

body.en:
The Nepal Tourism Board says 35 Australians are missing after a massive flood and landslide disaster on the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 273 people on Wednesday, with hundreds more unaccounted for.

That number had been 34 until the tourism board published an update Thursday afternoon.

Another 823 people, including 644 Nepali and foreign tourists, remained out of contact in Nepal, according to the country's disaster agency.

On Thursday afternoon, China's foreign minister said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were missing, revising down earlier reporting in Chinese state media that 558 people, including 260 foreigners, were missing in Gyirong Port, Tibet.

"At this point, there are 34 Australians who are missing," Albanese told a press conference on Thursday morning. "People would have seen some of the footage, which is a truly horrific event."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Albanese said it was difficult to obtain information from Nepali authorities and appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

"At this point, Nepal is a developing country. It doesn't have the resources that an event like that would have in Australia, so information is difficult.

"Our thoughts are with all those who will be concerned about their loved ones today."

Defence minister Penny Wong echoed the Prime Minister's statements, noting that the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) was working "urgently" to ascertain the welfare and location of the missing Australians.

"We are currently deploying further DFAT personnel, including crisis response experts to the region to ensure that we do provide the support needed to these posts, particularly our post in Nepal," Wong in a press conference on Thursday.

"At this stage, access and information are very limited given the scale of disaster. We will do our best, to ascertain whatever information we can."

A US-based tour company Himalayan Glacier Adventures told ABC News that 15 Australians, part of a group of 47 people, were on a hiking tour in the Lantang Valley at the time of the landslides.

The group of Australians was comprised of nine men and six women. Two of those Australians were reportedly boys aged 11 and 14, and a woman aged 64.

Tilak Pokharel, president of the Australian Nepalese Multicultural Centre, said there were "a lot" of people in Melbourne waiting anxiously to hear from loved ones.

"There are a lot of people affected by the flood. There are many people from that area living in Melbourne," Pokharel said.

reflection.en: The news of hundreds missing and entire settlements "wiped out" by floods and landslides in Nepal brings immense sorrow. In moments of such widespread devastation and loss of life, the brevity of "Jesus wept" reminds us that grief is a natural and holy response. Yahweh, in Christ, shares in our human pain, offering a compassionate presence when words fail.
reflection.zh: 尼泊尔洪水和山体滑坡造成数百人失踪、整个定居点“被夷为平地”的消息，带来了巨大的悲痛。在如此大规模的毁灭和生命损失面前，“雅伟哭了”这简短的经文提醒我们，悲伤是一种自然而神圣的回应。雅伟在基督里分担我们人类的痛苦，当言语无法表达时，祂提供了一个充满怜悯的同在。

verse.textEn: Jesus wept.
verse.textZh: 耶稣哭了。

title.en: 'Can't abstain from this debate': Pacific nations the next frontier in deep-sea mining
title.zh: “无法回避的辩论”：太平洋国家成为深海采矿的下一个前沿

summary.en: A new report warns that commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin as early as 2027, driven by increasing rivalry between the United States and China for critical minerals. Pacific nations are reportedly split between the promise of economic benefits and the risk of irreversible damage to the environment...
summary.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国之间对关键矿产的竞争日益加剧，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能最早在2027年开始。据报道，太平洋国家在经济利益的承诺与对环境和当地生计造成不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。

body.en:
Commercial deep-sea mining in the Pacific could begin in months without policy guardrails due to increasing rivalry between the United States and China over critical minerals, a new report warns.

Analysis by the Lowy Institute has found mining could start as early as 2027, with the floor of the Pacific Ocean holding vast quantities of prized resources.

The contest between the world's two biggest economies is being driven by demand created by batteries, weapons systems, and power grids.

The region's nations are split between the promise of economic spoils and the risk of irreversible damage to the ecosystem, fisheries, food security, livelihoods and culture, according to the research.

It argues the absence of an international governance framework for commercial deep-sea mining leaves Pacific states negotiating without internationally agreed protections.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

This also leaves them dependent on individual agreements drafted by companies seeking to mine their ocean floor.

"For the Pacific Island nations caught in the middle of this great power battle for critical mineral supremacy, the economic proposition is difficult to refuse," the Lowy Institute's Connor Graham writes.

"The problem is not that Pacific nations disagree, it is that they are being forced to negotiate individually against parties with vastly more resources, information, and legal capacity, and that the international framework designed to protect them has stalled."

Graham said while Australia was yet to take a clear position on deep-sea mining in the Pacific, it has the standing, relationships, and institutional presence to make an impact.

This includes its membership in the Pacific Islands Forum and as a long-standing ally of the US.

"A commitment to standards that have not been written as a condition for activity that is about to begin is less of a policy, and more of an abstention," he said.

Countries including Australia have started to enter into deals for critical minerals, which are crucial for a number for emerging technologies.

The federal government has announced a $1.2 billion critical minerals strategic reserve to secure the supply of key minerals deemed crucial for Australia's economy and national security.

body.zh: 一份新报告警告称，由于美国和中国在关键矿产方面的竞争日益激烈，太平洋地区的商业深海采矿可能会在没有政策保护的情况下在几个月内开始。 洛伊研究所的分析发现，采矿最早可能在 2027 年开始，太平洋海底蕴藏着大量珍贵资源。 全球最大的两个经济体之间的竞争是由电池、武器系统和电网产生的需求驱动的。 研究表明，该地区各国在经济收益的承诺和生态系统、渔业、粮食安全、生计和文化遭受不可逆转损害的风险之间存在分歧。 它认为，商业深海采矿国际治理框架的缺乏导致太平洋国家在没有国际商定保护的情况下进行谈判。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 这也使得它们依赖于寻求海底采矿的公司起草的单独协议。 洛伊研究所的康纳·格雷厄姆写道：“对于陷入这场争夺关键矿产霸权的大国战争的太平洋岛国来说，这个经济提议很难拒绝。” “问题不在于太平洋国家不同意，而在于它们被迫与拥有更多资源、信息和法律能力的各方进行单独谈判，而旨在保护它们的国际框架已经陷入停滞。” 格雷厄姆表示，虽然澳大利亚尚未对太平洋深海采矿采取明确立场，但它拥有产生影响的地位、关系和机构存在。 这包括它是太平洋岛屿论坛的成员以及美国的长期盟友。 他说：“对尚未作为即将开始的活动条件的标准的承诺与其说是一项政策，不如说是一种弃权。” 包括澳大利亚在内的国家已开始签订关键矿物交易，这对许多新兴技术至关重要。 联邦政府宣布设立 12 亿美元的关键矿产战略储备，以确保对澳大利亚经济和国家安全至关重要的关键矿产的供应。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

As the report warns of mining commencing without adequate policy guardrails, the words of 1 Corinthians 10:23 remind us that while many actions may be permissible, not all are truly...
reflection.zh: 太平洋深海采矿的前景给岛屿国家带来了严峻的选择，需要在潜在的经济收益与不可逆转的生态破坏风险之间取得平衡。正如报告警告，在缺乏充分政策保障的情况下，采矿可能即将开始，哥林多前书10:23提醒我们，虽然许多事情是合法的，但并非所有事情都有益处或能造就人。这种情况呼唤智慧，以辨别什么能真正造就社区并保护雅伟的创造，而不是仅仅追求权宜之计。

title.en: A teenager's death has prompted fresh calls for relationship education
title.zh: 一名青少年的死亡引发了对人际关系教育的新呼声

summary.en: A 16-year-old girl was found unresponsive at a home on Sydney's Northern Beaches on Sunday but died in hospital on Tuesday.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A teenage girl's tragic death, which has been reported as being linked to sexual choking, has sparked high-profile calls for broadened relationship education.

A 16-year-old girl was found unresponsive at an Elanora Heights home, on Sydney's Northern Beaches, on Sunday.

Police declined to confirm reports detectives were investigating sexual choking as a possible factor in the death.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Independent MP Zali Steggall mentioned the reports after a National Cabinet meeting on Wednesday affirmed a commitment to ending gender-based violence.

She said agreed measures were weak and pushed for more action, including a respectful relationship education campaign.

"My call for a national education campaign has been underscored by the devastating news today of the death of a 16-year-old Northern Beaches girl," Steggall said in a statement.

"My thoughts are with her family, friends and community at this incredibly difficult time."

Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek said there was no safe way to engage in choking.

"I'm sure I've said it to you in the past almost 60 per cent of young people report they've experienced choking in a recent sexual encounter," she told ABC Radio on Thursday morning.

"I can't say anything, obviously, about this tragic situation in NSW ... but in general terms, figures like that just concern me so deeply.

"There is no safe way of choking someone. Parents have to use this opportunity to talk to their young people."

A survey of 4702 Australians between 18 and 35 in 2024 found 57 per cent of respondents had been choked during sex at least once.

One-third of those respondents reported it occurring for the first time between 19 and 21.

The report's co-author noted choking in a sexual context could lead to serious brain injuries, including memory loss and issues with problem-solving.

"It doesn't matter if there are no apparent injuries, or whether the person consented," Professor Heather Douglas said at the time.

"Brain injury can also be incremental — getting a bit worse with each choking — and the person may not know they have suffered a brain injury. The effects of repeated strangling are insidious and build over time."

title.en: Australia wants more data centres. A disagreement over power sources stands in the way
title.zh: 澳大利亚需要更多的数据中心。电源问题上的分歧阻碍了

summary.en: Proposed legislation to force data centre developers to provide their own renewable energy sources has run into resistance.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two jurisdictions have forced the prime minister to back down on a major policy that would have required all new AI data centres to be powered by renewable energy rather than coal and gas.

Anthony Albanese left the door open at a meeting of the nation's leaders on Wednesday to a more "flexible" approach as Queensland and the Northern Territory refused to agree to standards requiring them to use renewables for new data centre developments.

He announced the agreement on the AI laws alongside domestic violence measures and firearm reforms following a meeting of National Cabinet in Sydney.

"We want to make sure that in attracting investment, we don't have eight different systems operating around the country," he said on Wednesday.

"That's why we came to a common position, which recognises that all states aren't exactly the same, and that was accommodated in the way that we normally do in a flexible way."

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas said the nation's leaders agreed renewables would be the main form of energy to power future data centres in Australia.

"Acknowledging that there are different circumstances through the fact that in Queensland, for instance, they have state-owned generation," he told ABC's 7.30 on Wednesday.

"So there's no need for the federal government to use its powers that it has to override what states want."

Gregor Verbic, an energy expert at Sydney University, said the national grid was facing the imminent closure of multiple coal-fired power stations.

"(It) will leave a huge gap in the generation capacity, and we are not building new capacity fast enough," he told the Australian Associated Press news agency.

The federal government has proposed legislation to force data centre developers to provide their own renewable energy source.

Both the Queensland and NT governments provided considerable pushback, with the final national agreement failing to mention renewable energy directly.

Verbic said ensuring the energy brought online is renewable is essential to meet Australia's emissions reduction targets.

Albanese flagged draft legislation will be introduced by the end of 2026, with the aim for it to be passed in early 2027.

For the latest from SBS News, download our app and subscribe to our newsletter .
body.zh: 两个司法管辖区迫使总理放弃一项重大政策，该政策要求所有新的人工智能数据中心均由可再生能源而不是煤炭和天然气供电。 由于昆士兰州和北领地拒绝同意要求他们使用可再生能源进行新数据中心开发的标准，安东尼·阿尔博内斯在周三的国家领导人会议上为采取更“灵活”的方法敞开了大门。 在悉尼举行的国家内阁会议后，他宣布就人工智能法以及家庭暴力措施和枪支改革达成协议。 “我们希望确保在吸引投资时，我们不会在全国各地运营八个不同的系统，”他周三表示。 “这就是为什么我们达成了共同立场，承认所有州并不完全相同，并且我们以通常灵活的方式进行了适应。” 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 南澳大利亚州州长 Peter Malinauskas 表示，国家领导人同意可再生能源将成为澳大利亚未来数据中心供电的主要能源形式。 “承认存在不同的情况，例如在昆士兰州，他们有国有发电，”他周三告诉美国广播公司的 7.30。 “因此，联邦政府没有必要使用其权力来推翻各州的意愿。” 悉尼大学能源专家Gregor Verbic表示，国家电网面临着多个燃煤发电站即将关闭的问题。 他告诉澳大利亚美联社：“这将在发电能力方面留下巨大缺口，而我们建设新能力的速度不够快。” 联邦政府已提议立法，迫使数据中心开发商提供自己的可再生能源。 昆士兰州和北领地政府都提出了相当大的阻力，最终的国家协议没有直接提及可再生能源。 韦尔比克表示，确保上网能源是可再生能源对于实现澳大利亚的减排目标至关重要。 阿尔巴尼亚提出的立法草案将于 2026 年底提出，目标是在 2027 年初获得通过。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

title.en: Albanese reveals humanitarian visa intake won't be cut, amid migration reform questions
title.zh: 阿尔巴内斯透露，由于移民改革问题，人道主义签证的接收量不会减少

summary.en: Labor has been signalling an upcoming shift in migration policy, as the prime minister quelled speculation on a key detail.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Albanese government has denied plans to slash Australia’s humanitarian intake by a third, after reports the cut was being considered as part of a broader push to reduce net overseas migration.

On Thursday, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said in a statement the government's 20,000 humanitarian placements would "be continued in future years, consistent with Australia’s humanitarian commitments".

The statement followed reporting on Thursday morning by The Australian Financial Review newspaper that Labor appeared poised to reduce humanitarian placements from 20,000 to 13,750 at the start of the next financial year and that it had factored the decrease into migration forecasts.

A spokesman for Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke told SBS News earlier on Thursday that the final decision on next year's humanitarian intake had not yet been made and linked the process to next year's budget. At the time he did not rule out cuts.

But in his statement to SBS News, Albanese said the existing figure "remains government policy".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In the wake of multiple international conflicts around the world, Labor has made a series of increases to the humanitarian intake, pushing it to its current high.

The confusion comes as the government is anticipated to announce an overhaul of its migration policy.

Labor had been expected to reveal details in a National Press Club address by Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke earlier this month, but the speech was cancelled after Burke failed to secure cabinet agreement on the best approach.

Since then, Albanese has refused to give further updates, telling ABC radio on Tuesday that there are a "series of plans in place" but there is still "more work to do" to finalise them. He declined to set a timeframe for immigration announcements, saying only that they would come at "appropriate times".

Migration targets have been the source of recent public debate, with One Nation pushing a tough anti-migration stance and gaining in the polls.

Both major parties have sought to restrict their own immigration policies while denying that this is in response to the minor party's growing popularity.

Opposition leader Angus Taylor has said the Coalition will cap net overseaos migration (NOM) at or below the number of homes built in Australia the previous year. Current building rates suggest their figure would be under 180,000; however, the Coalition is yet to announce where they would restrict immigration to reach that figure.
